title: Pre-audit sanity kit: RBACv2 + SIEM export
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, hands-on pre-audit "sanity kit" for RBACv2, audit log export schema, and evidence automation feeding the SIEM. Intended for the on-call compliance owner and the SRE/infra engineer who will run the dry-run with an auditor or internal assessor.

Scope and assumptions:
- Controls targeted: SOC 2 CC6/CC7-ish (access controls, logging, monitoring) and relevant ISO 27001 Annex A mappings.
- Systems: auth service (RBACv2), audit-export service, evidence-automation pipeline, SIEM ingest (logs-redwood-siem).
- This doc is an operational checklist + quick Q&A; it is NOT the canonical control-mapping artifacts (see linked Confluence).

Quick checklist (5–10 minute smoke):
1) RBAC health check (rbacv2):
   - Confirm RBAC migration job status: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://infra-api.internal/rbacv2/migration/status -> expect "completed"
   - Sample permission check: run impersonation test for a canary user (dev-canary@example.com) -> ensure allowed and denied actions align with policy matrix.
   - Random spot-check: pick 3 high-priv roles (admin, platform-ops, billing) and verify membership lists exported in last 24h.

2) Audit log export sanity (last 24h):
   - Trigger/export a 24h slice from audit-exports service:
     curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"range":"24h","format":"jsonl"}' https://audit-exports.internal/exports -> capture job id
   - Validate sample line contains required fields: timestamp, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, request_id, kv_cache_present (if relevant).
   - Expected example (single-line JSON): {"ts":"2025-10-14T18:22:33Z","actor_id":"user:alice@redwood.ai","actor_role":"platform-ops","action":"deploy:model","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"m-12345","outcome":"success","request_id":"req_8f1a"}

3) SIEM ingest verification:
   - Confirm recent export landed in S3/ingest-bucket and SIEM connector mark: s3://evidence-exports/2025-10-14/*.jsonl
   - Check SIEM mapping: field "actor_role" mapped to siem.actor.role, timestamp -> @timestamp, request_id -> siem.request.id.
   - Query SIEM for a known request_id and verify enrichment (geo/ip/user-agent) exists.

4) Evidence automation pipeline smoke (evidence-automation):
   - Kick a dry-run job: /jobs/dryrun?export-id=<recent> and watch logs for failures in transform step.
   - Verify checksum/hash and retention-tagging metadata attached to exported artifact (metadata: export_hash, exported_by, retention_days).
   - Confirm the evidence manifest file is created (manifest.jsonl) and includes record counts matching upload.

Control mapping quick notes (how to explain to auditor):
- RBACv2 coverage: role-based policies cover admin/ops/customer-facing/readonly. We maintain role->permission matrix in repo infra/rbac/policies and generate daily snapshots to evidence storage.
- Audit logs: immutable append-only JSONL files written to our write-once S3 prefix with object-lock TTL aligned to retention policy; each object has server-side signature metadata for tamper detection.
- SIEM export: ingestion uses a signed transfer token and checksum verification; SIEM index mapping preserves raw and normalized fields for auditor search.

Common auditor Qs and suggested short answers (tone: factual, nontechnical where possible):
Q: How do you ensure access reviews are performed?
A: We run weekly automated role membership snapshots and surface anomalies in a Slack channel for managers. Quarterly, managers confirm memberships via the access-review workflow (Jira ticket). Evidence: monthly snapshot files + approval ticket IDs.

Q: How do you prove that a given action was performed by an authorized user?
A: Each audit log entry includes actor_id (SSO subject), actor_role (from RBACv2 service), and request_id correlated across infra traces. We can export the JSONL slice for a time window plus the RBAC snapshot in effect at that timestamp.

Q: What stops an attacker or admin from altering logs?
A: Logs are written to a dedicated write-only bucket with restricted keys. Exports are immutable (object-lock in WORM mode for retention period) and we publish daily checksums to a protected ledger. We also maintain an ingest-proof in SIEM with transfer signatures.

Q: How do you map logs to SOC2 control criteria?
A: We keep a mapping table (Confluence) that links audit fields to control criteria (e.g., actor_id -> CC6.1, outcome -> CC7.1). For the dry-run we export that mapping as a CSV and attach it to the evidence bundle.

Evidence packaging checklist for handoff to auditor:
- RBAC snapshot created at export time (rbac-snapshot-2025-10-14.json).
- Exported audit logs (audit-export-2025-10-14.jsonl) + manifest and checksum.
- Evidence manifest: manifest-2025-10-14.json (list of files, counts, hashes).
- SIEM ingestion proof: siem-ingest-notes-2025-10-14.txt (ingest ID, time, connector logs).
- Access-review tickets referenced (list of Jira IDs).

Sanity tests to run with auditor present (priority order):
1) Pick a recent action reported by auditor (or create a reproducible action) and follow it across RBAC snapshot -> audit-export -> SIEM index.
2) Demonstrate export immutability: show object metadata and checksum, then show ledger entry for checksum.
3) Run an access-review sample: manager approval sign-off for a user and evidence ticket.

Open risks / unresolved items (to call out):
- Export schema v2 fields (resource_labels) not yet included in all old audit producers (gap ticket: JIRA SEC-558). Plan: backfill transformation in automation.
- Retention policy automation: some archival transitions still manual for legacy buckets (ownership ticket: INFRA-334).

Action items (owners):
- Nora: run full dry-run and attach artifacts to demo bundle (due 2025-10-20).
- Ethan: validate SIEM field mapping and create a small Kibana dashboard for sample queries (due 2025-10-22).
- Priya: update the Confluence control mapping CSV to include latest schema fields (due 2025-10-21).

Notes to self / quick commands:
- Export job list: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://audit-exports.internal/jobs | jq .
- Download artifact: aws s3 cp s3://evidence-exports/2025-10-14/audit-export-*.jsonl ./
- Verify manifest counts: cat manifest-2025-10-14.json | jq .record_counts

Appendix: sample SIEM query (KQL-like) to locate evidence quickly:
- siem.index: "redwood-audit-*" AND siem.request.id: "req_8f1a" | project @timestamp, siem.actor.name, siem.actor.role, event.action, event.outcome

This doc is deliberately compact. For the canonical mapping artifacts and finalized attestation pack see the linked Confluence page and the formal evidence repo. If you hit anything flaky during the dry-run, paste error logs into JIRA SEC-421 and ping @sec-oncall in Slack.

-- Samira (prep owner)
